ctx.x: And in the liner notes, he mentioned the fact that Chico Hamilton, the drummer, had mentioned on an interview that they had together on the radio in Chicago some time back that there was a guy out in California who was playing the way the guys are playing now a long time ago. In fact, the only thing he had heard really change a lot was the saxophone players, you know. And he was talking about I had been playing this type of horn that became popular later on a long time ago. He heard me playing it out here.

Because he was from here. This was his home. In fact, right after I first came out, he was in the Navy, and they had a band together down at the Downbeat Club with John Anderson and Buddy Collette and Red Callender, and I think Gerry Wiggins might have been with that band, the great... yeah, I think he might have been with that band -- and Britt Woodman on trombone. And later on, I heard the Honey Dripper band, Joe Liggins and His Honey Drippers. They became real popular, and they used to work the Downbeat Club…
And while we're still talking about Central Avenue, I'd like to mention about the Lincoln Theatre. Do you remember the Lincoln Theatre?
